title: a statement-position switch keeps ordinary TypeScript behavior, and over a literal-typed scrutinee that behavior is TS2678 for a case label the scrutinee can never equal
notes: CORRECTED by C17 — this case previously declared `expect: output` with ["a,b"], and the JS reference only appeared to satisfy it because `conformance/runner/backend-js.mjs` never ran `checkEmittedProject`; the frontend's own acceptance (`compileAndCheckProject`, and the `smithers` CLI via `checkEmittedTypeScript`) rejects this program. Four implementations were measured on this exact source and all report TS2678 at 7:10: stock typescript@7.0.2 from npm (`tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2022`), typescript-js@5.9.3 (the library `checkEmittedTypeScript` itself uses), the JS reference through the fixed harness (mapped back through the compiler's own source map), and the pinned Go fork through `--backend go`. C14 additionally measured a pristine, zero-patch fork checkout: same TS2678 at 7:10. The rule is not about fallthrough at all: `switch ("a")` gives the scrutinee the literal type `"a"`, so `case "b"` is not comparable to it. Two control probes pin the mechanism — the same switch with `break` in every clause and no fallthrough still reports TS2678, and widening the scrutinee to a `string` parameter compiles clean. The locked compatibility rule (docs/DECISIONS.md; docs/src/pages/specification/compatibility.mdx) is that syntax shared with TypeScript keeps TypeScript's behavior unless a divergence is explicitly documented, so reporting TS2678 SATISFIES the rule and suppressing it would BE the divergence. Fallthrough itself is still pinned, over a scrutinee TypeScript accepts, by the sibling case `statement-switch-fallthrough-over-a-widened-scrutinee`.
